hero.title: Master’s in Chemical Engineering in Switzerland for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: A Master’s in Chemical Engineering in Switzerland is a great choice for those interested in chemical processes, process design, biotechnology, material science, energy systems and sustainable industrial production. Swiss universities provide advanced scientific education coupled with research in chemical reaction engineering, separation processes, polymers and environmental technologies.

overview: The Chemical and Bioengineering program at ETH Zurich normally takes 1.5 years (90 ECTS credits). The Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology program at EPFL is made up of 120 ECTS credits and is typically designed as a two-year degree.
### 2\. Yes, Indian students can study Chemical Engineering in English medium.

Yes indeed. Both ETH Zurich’s Chemical and Bioengineering and EPFL’s Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology programs are taught in English. Applicants must still satisfy the relevant language requirements.

sections.title: How long is a Master's in Chemical Engineering in Switzerland?
sections.lead: The Chemical and Bioengineering program at ETH Zurich normally takes 1.5 years (90 ECTS credits). The Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology program at EPFL is made up of 120 ECTS credits and is typically designed as a two-year degree.

items: ### 2\. Yes, Indian students can study Chemical Engineering in English medium.

Yes indeed. Both ETH Zurich’s Chemical and Bioengineering and EPFL’s Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology programs are taught in English. Applicants must still satisfy the relevant language requirements.
### 3\. What is the estimated cost of the full program?

The budget as per the estimates in this guide is about ₹31.81–52.27 lakh for 1.5 years at ETH Zurich or ₹42.42–69.70 lakh for two years at EPFL. Actual costs will vary according to tuition category, accommodation and personal spending.
### 4\. I have Bachelor’s in Biotechnology/Chemistry, can I apply?

Possibly, depending on the program and your academic background. You can do a lot of engineering classes in chemical engineering programs . Some of the related programs may be more suited to chemistry or biotechnology degrees . Please check the official eligibility criteria before applying.
### 5\. Can I work in Switzerland after my studies?

Sure, that could happen. But you won't get hired automatically. Graduates are required to find suitable employment and to comply with the relevant Swiss immigration and work-permit requirements. Consider relevant technical skills, internships and language proficiency to improve competitiveness.
